messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — seeing p95/p99 climb on rtx-pool for short-seq (<128) requests since the kernel roll last night. Heatmap shows a long tail in queue wait + KV-miss spikes. link: https://redwood.internal/heatmaps/rtx-shortseq

maria: Numbers? rough p50/p95/p99 and qps? also which pool and model?

alex: p50 ~ 28ms, p95 ~ 230ms, p99 ~ 510ms. QPS steady, actually throughput down ~12% for this workload. Pool: rtx-16-dynbatch, model: gptx-3-small (open).

cheng: I profiled a couple of samples. Two interesting things: (1) kernel selector sometimes falls back to the generic attention kernel for short sequences due to alignment/packed-kv assumptions; that adds ~40-60ms per request in the tail. (2) KV cache miss ratio increased ~8% after the storage TTL tweak, causing extra memfetches from host.

sam: Could be scheduler interaction too — continuous batching max_wait_ms was bumped to 8ms in that rollout. For small sequences that increases microbatching variance and pushes some requests into larger batches causing cross-request cache evictions.

alex: Repro config snippet from runtime: ```yaml
scheduler:
  continuous_batching: true
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_wait_ms: 8
  prefer_latency: false
```

maria: So tradeoff: higher max_wait reduces cpu/gpu overhead and raises throughput but hurts tail for tiny seqs. We need p95 SLO at 200ms, p99 at 400ms for this customer. Current is above.

cheng: Proposed quick experiments (safe):
1) lower max_wait_ms -> 3ms for rtx-16-dynbatch (fast path for short-seq).
2) bump max_batch_tokens -> 8192 (to absorb bursts without increasing wait).
3) force kernel pinning for short-seq models to use fused-attention kernel: `--kernel-policy=prefer:fused-attn` for canary.
Run A/B for 2 hours.

sam: Note: (2) might increase average batch size and thus avg latency; we should watch p50 too. Also bumping max_batch_tokens interacts with preemption on dedicated nodes.

alex: I tried a local canary: max_wait_ms=3 reduced p95 to ~185ms and p99 to ~370ms, throughput dropped 4% but steadier. With kernel pinning p95 improved another ~25ms. KV-miss still a problem at p99.

maria: Good. We should coordinate with storage team on TTL rollback or targeted pinning to avoid cold-evictions. @cheng can you add a metric tag for kv_miss_rate and a tail-latency heatmap per microbatch-size?

cheng: Yep — will push a probe that emits per-request microbatch_size + kv_hit boolean and create a p99 heatmap grouped by microbatch_size. Query will be `trace.metric:kvmiss_ratio{pool=rtx-16-dynbatch} by microbatch_size`.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled by cheng: canary config update to rtx-16-dynbatch on 2026-03-18T02:30Z -> changes: max_wait_ms 8 -> 3, kernel-policy: prefer:fused-attn. CI: passed, rollout CI: 10%.

maria: Run the rollout to 10% and collect for 2h. If p95 < 200 && p99 < 400 and throughput loss < 6% we promote. Otherwise roll back. Also watch kv_miss_rate and memfetch latency.

sam: If kv_miss_rate stays high we can try a short-lived prefetch for frequent prefixes (cheap LRU warming). That should reduce p99 without touching batcher.

alex: Also found a small regression in the last kernel patch (commit 0a1b2c) that added an extra memcpy when switching quantization path; opened PR to remove the memcpy for short-seq path. That plus the scheduler tweak should fix most of tail.

cheng: Test plan uploaded: short-seq canary -> 10% -> 2h -> collect: p50/p95/p99, throughput, microbatch distribution, kv_hit_ratio, kernel_fallback_count, memcopy_time. I’ll tag the dashboards.

maria: Thanks. After the canary, if metrics look good, schedule a cluster-wide rollout during low traffic window.

alex: TL;DR: reducing max_wait_ms + kernel pinning helps tail at small cost to throughput; KV warmup + removing memcpy fix will reduce p99 further. Will post results in ~3h. :thumbsup:
